To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BARS has been expressed in E. coli as a truncated form and crystallized in the space group P6 (2) (2)22/P 6 (4) 22.
we have crystallized a truncated version of the enzyme brefeldin-A ADP-ribosylated substrate, which is involved in membrane fision.
the truncated form of BARNs has been expressed in Escherichio coli, purified and successfully crystallized, and that SeMet-labeled protein has been crystallized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterization of BARS.
the elucidation of the structure-function relationships of the BARS enzyme.
the elucidation of the three-dimensional structure of BARS and its interaction with the membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BARS is the first ADP-ribosylation factor (ARF)-GTPase-activated protein that can be crystallized and studied by X-ray crystallography.
the BARS structure has been solved at 2.2 A resolution.
the crystallization of a protein is a complex process that depends on a large number of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystallization conditions are suitable for the crystallization of the full-length BARS and that the crystals are isomorphous with the crystals of truncated BARS.
the BARS crystal belongs to space group P4(1)2(1) or P4(3)2(1), with unit-cell parameters of a = b = c = 88.8 A, alpha = gamma = beta = 900.
BARS is a good candidate for the determination of its three-dimensional structure at atomic resolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BARS is amenable to structural studies and that the C-terminus is not essential to crystallize the enzyme.
the crystallization of a protein can be improved by using SeMet-substitution, even in the absence of any specific SeMet-binding site in the protein structure.

the C-terminal region of BARS, which has been shown to interact with the cytosolic leaflet of the Golgi membrane and to mediate its fission, does not appear to be required for the enzymatic activity of BARS.
